summary: Hay Airport serves the remote town of Hay in the far south-west of New South Wales, Australia, situated on the Hay Plain, one of the flattest landforms in the world. The airport supports general aviation and serves as a useful stopover for private pilots traversing the vast inland distances between Adelaide and Sydney. Its classification as a medium airport reflects a longer-than-typical runway for the sparsely populated region, accommodating both charter and emergency service operations.
faqs:
Q: Where is Hay Airport located?
A: Hay Airport is located near the town of Hay in the Riverina region of far south-western New South Wales, Australia, roughly 300 km west of Wagga Wagga.

Q: Does Hay Airport have scheduled passenger services?
A: No, Hay Airport does not currently have regular scheduled passenger flights. It primarily serves general aviation, charter operations, and emergency services.

Q: What is the nearest major airport to Hay?
A: Griffith Airport is the closest commercial-service airport, located about 130 km to the east, while Mildura Airport and Wagga Wagga Airport are also within reach for larger air connections.

Q: Is pilot training conducted at Hay Airport?
A: The flat surrounding terrain and open airspace make the Hay area attractive for cross-country training flights, though formal flight schools are not based on the field.
transport_tips: The airport sits a few kilometres south of Hay town centre and is most easily reached by car or taxi along the local road network. Hay itself is connected by the Mid-Western and Cobb Highways, making road access straightforward from Griffith, Balranald, or Deniliquin. Travellers should arrange ground transport in advance, as rental car and taxi options are limited in this remote rural area.
local_tip: Pilots stopping at Hay should note that the surrounding Hay Plain offers exceptionally clear skies and flat emergency landing options, but also means weather can change quickly during summer thunderstorm season, so always carry extra fuel reserves and check the windsock before committing to the strip.
